subject: Sizing vs. H100 memory slab — Crestline dedicated commit options
messages:

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options / GPU mix question

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo — the throughput numbers looked good. Can you also show how commit tiers (12mo v 24mo) change effective $/token and whether we can reserve “hot” H100 slots with burst credits?

Procurement copied for cadence. Attaching a short procurement template.

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-09T11:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity options / GPU mix question

Aditya / Vivek — forwarding Crestline's ask. Key asks: perf/$ matrix A100-40G vs H100-80G vs L40S for a 20-slot reserved pool, 12v24 month commit modeling, and whether we can provide a capped burst buffer for H100s (they want some hot capacity). They also want 99th percentile tail SLA numbers.

Notes: Crestline’s workload is low-latency chat + long-context embeddings (avg prompt 1.2k tokens, kv cache heavy). My quick take: H100 wins on perf for long-context and NVL (perf/slot), but A100-40G with more slots may offer better perf/$ for moderate context. L40S might be the sweet spot for inference-memory heavy workloads if we can quantize. Need concrete numbers.

Can you run two scenario sheets:
- Scenario A: 20 H100-80G reserved slots (baseline list price, our standard reserved discount tiers)
- Scenario B: mixed pool 8 H100 + 12 A100 with hot-H100 burst credits (define burst credit policy)
- Scenario C: 24 L40S slots as cost-optimized option with per-model quantization plan

Please include: raw throughput (tokens/sec per slot), estimated token $ at expected utilization (assume 65% avg util), 99th pct latency targets for 4k and 32k context, and recommended commit term and discount. Also note any constraints (multi-tenant vs dedicated GPU isolation).

Kimberly — procurement will push on price and SLA; if we propose deeper TCV discounts we should pre-approve approval matrix.

Laura
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-10T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity options / GPU mix question

Attaching quick scenario outputs — see pricing_model_breakdown.xlsx (attached). High level:
- 20x H100-80G: best raw throughput for 32k context. Estimated perf/$ (token cost) is ~1.0x baseline (highest unit $ but fewer slots needed). 99th pct tail w/ our current placement: 110–140ms (4k) and 420–520ms (32k) at 65% util with continuous batching.
- Mixed pool (8 H100 + 12 A100-40G): perf/$ improves ~0.78x vs all-H100 because A100 slots are cheaper; for short-context requests we route to A100, long-context to H100. Tail: 95–125ms (4k) and 380–460ms (32k). Complexity: routing + rollback policy needed.
- 24x L40S: lowest $/slot; perf/$ estimated ~0.65x vs all-H100 but memory constraints mean quantization + sharding work for 32k models; tail latency for 32k is worse without model surgery.

Commit terms: 12mo commit gives ~18% off list for H100; 24mo commit pushes to ~25% plus a modest upfront credit. We can trade commit length for a small additional burst buffer (e.g., 15% burst credits for first 6 months) to be reserved for H100 hot slots.

Risks/caveats included in sheet.

—Aditya
Principal Solutions Eng, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Morton <alice@crestline.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@crestline.ai
Date: 2027-12-11T14:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options / GPU mix question

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick clarifications before we share with finance:
1) For the mixed pool, how do you guarantee latency for the short tail during model routing? We can’t have cold H100 fallbacks.
2) For 24mo commit with burst credits, can you convert unused burst credits to overage credit for subsequent quarters? Procurement asks for some fungibility.
3) Can you give an example SLA addendum line for 99th pct latency on 4k context at 65% util (we want something we can push upstream).

Procurement requests a redline-friendly MAT; they attached their template earlier. Once we have a clear price cadence and SLA text we can route to legal.

—Alice

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Alice Morton <alice@crestline.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-12T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options / GPU mix question

Alice — appreciate the clarifying questions. Responses inline: 

1) Mixed-pool routing guarantees: we implement a routing policy with two protections — (a) per-request SLO gating (if predicted latency >X route only to H100), and (b) pre-warming KV cache + pinned model instances for hot prefixes. Together these reduce cold-fallbacks to <0.5% of requests. We'll include a canary rollout plan and a clause that performance guarantees apply when routing policy is active.

2) Burst credits fungibility: for a 24mo commit we can allow conversion of up to 30% of unused burst credits in a quarter into a one-time overage credit applied to the next quarter (not cumulative). We'll put a clear cap and audit trail in the MAT redline.

3) SLA example line (draft): 
"99th percentile latency for 4k context shall be <= 140ms at 65% cluster utilization for covered models. Failure to meet this SLA for two consecutive measurement windows entitles Customer to a service credit equal to 5% of monthly committed fees."

I attached a short MAT redline that incorporates the above and the pricing scenarios (crestline_MAT_proposal_v1.pdf). If this looks good to you, Laura / Kimberly, we can present the pricing + SLA + DocuSign link to Crestline legal next week.

—Vivek
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
